Albania:
Hidden Gems

Beyond the familiar routes lie stone-built towns, clear-water springs and quiet mountain valleys. Discover three remarkable places and the stories that make them special.

Explore the hidden gems ↓
A place of contrasts

Small country.
Big stories.

Albania is a country in southeastern Europe, where the Adriatic and Ionian seas meet the mountains of the Balkans. Its landscape changes quickly: from the coast to green valleys and rugged alpine peaks.

This project looks beyond the best-known destinations. Meet three places that reveal Albania’s history, natural beauty and local traditions.

Historic town · Southern Albania

Gjirokastër

Stone roofs, Ottoman-era houses and a castle above the Drinos Valley.

A city shaped by stone

Step into the “Stone City.”

Gjirokastër sits on a steep hillside in the Drinos River valley in southern Albania. Its old town is known for grey stone roofs and distinctive houses that climb the slope toward the citadel. The historic centre is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property “Historic Centres of Berat and Gjirokastra.”

Many of the town’s traditional tower houses, locally known as kule, were built in the 17th century. Their thick stone walls and multi-level design helped families live through both cold winters and hot summers. A bazaar, mosque and churches also tell part of the town’s story.

Where it is

Southern Albania, in the Drinos River valley.

Look for

The 13th-century citadel, the old bazaar and traditional tower houses.

Why visit

For a close look at historic Balkan and Ottoman-era architecture.

What makes it a hidden gem?

Gjirokastër feels like a town built into the landscape. Its sloping lanes, stone rooftops and hilltop castle create a striking view, while the old neighbourhoods preserve the atmosphere of a living historic town.

Photo: Gjirokastër travel photo. Historical details: UNESCO World Heritage Centre.

Natural spring · Near Sarandë

The Blue Eye

Syri i Kaltër — a vivid spring surrounded by forest.

A natural wonder

Water in the shape of an eye.

The Blue Eye, called Syri i Kaltër in Albanian, is a natural spring near the village of Muzinë in southern Albania, about 18 kilometres from Sarandë. Water rises from an underground source into a pool surrounded by green woodland.

Its deep blue centre and lighter green-blue edges create the impression of a large eye. The spring is a protected natural monument and one of the region’s best-known nature stops.

Where it is

Near Muzinë, approximately 18 km from Sarandë.

Look for

The deep blue centre, turquoise water and surrounding forest.

Why visit

To see a striking spring and enjoy the quiet woodland setting.

What makes it a hidden gem?

The spring’s unusual colours look almost unreal, but they are part of a real natural landscape. Follow the paths around the forest and take time to notice how the water changes colour in the light.

Photo and place information: Albanian Blue Eye destination page. Location details: Albanian National Tourism Agency.

Mountain village · Northern Albania

Theth

A quiet alpine village surrounded by the rugged Albanian Alps.

Life in the highlands

A village among the peaks.

Theth lies in a remote valley in northern Albania’s Albanian Alps. The village is known for its dramatic mountain scenery and its old stone houses, and it offers a glimpse of a traditional way of life shaped by the highlands.

Nearby natural attractions include Grunas Waterfall, Grunas Canyon and the Okoli Cold Springs. Mountain trails connect the village with the surrounding valleys and peaks, making Theth a starting point for walks through the alpine landscape.

Where it is

Northern Albania, in a valley of the Albanian Alps.

Look for

Grunas Waterfall, Grunas Canyon and Okoli Cold Springs.

Why visit

For mountain scenery, village heritage and outdoor walks.

What makes it a hidden gem?

Theth offers a completely different view of Albania from its coast and historic southern towns. Here, steep peaks, green meadows and village life set the pace. The journey through the mountains is part of the experience.

Photo: Wikimedia Commons. Place details: Albanian National Tourism Agency.
